text:
maya: saw a flood of node NotReady alerts in syd1 ~10m ago, GPU pools (g4dn) dropping and control-plane heartbeats flaky. Pod evictions starting.

oncall-bot: Incident alert triggered: region=syd1 severity=prod-impacting - paging oncall.

elaine: I'm on it. @maya can you paste the top failing node output and any control-plane logs you have?

maya: copying snippets.
```
$ kubectl --context=syd1 get nodes | grep -E 'NotReady|Ready'
ip-10-1-8-12   NotReady   2d    v1.27.3
ip-10-1-9-45   NotReady   4m    v1.27.3
ip-10-1-7-33   NotReady   3m    v1.27.3
ip-10-1-6-21   Ready      10d   v1.27.3
```

maya: and a `kubectl describe node ip-10-1-9-45` shows repeated CNI errors and kubelet reporting inability to reach API server.

samir: seeing BGP session flaps to our edge routers for syd1 around the same time window. Provider status page shows intermittent network instability in the AZ.

sourav: autoscaler logs show scale-downs failed and then rapid scale-ups kicked in, a bunch of pods are pending due to tainted nodes. Looks like the control-plane lost connectivity to kubelets -> we got split brain-ish behaviour.

elaine: ok plan: 1) mark syd1 as degraded and stop new allocations 2) trigger traffic shift for realtime inference routes to sfo1 with 20% gradual cutover 3) fire up dedicated-burst in sfo1 for critical tenants 4) open incident ticket and customer notifications.

maya: running command to cordon/evict unhealthy GPU nodes now:
```
kubectl --context=syd1 get nodes -o name | xargs -n1 kubectl --context=syd1 cordon
for n in ip-10-1-9-45 ip-10-1-7-33; do kubectl --context=syd1 drain $n --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force & done
```

deploy-bot: Runbook `regional-failover` started by @elaine. Step 2: adjust traffic weights.

samir: Confirmed upstream: multiple BGP peers flapping, ASN-to-ASN keepalive drops. Network team opened provider ticket (PROV-9872).

elaine: @sourav can you start the sfo1 capacity bump? Estimate cost delta? Need rough number to approve emergency spend.

sourav: spinning up 6 x p4d-equivalent in sfo1 dedicated-burst. Estimated monthly delta if left for 24/7 ~ $36k, but we can tear down after stabilization. Hourly emergency window cost ~ $50/hr.

maya: pushing a temporary routing rule to route inference traffic to sfo1 for `realtime` and `critical` labels. Will keep batch jobs in syd1 paused.

elaine: on customer comms: draft message in #status-updates: "We are experiencing a regional networking issue impacting inference in syd1. Traffic is being shifted to alternate regions, we are enabling emergency capacity. No data loss expected. We'll update in 30m."

oncall-bot: Incident INC-4521 created, severity=high, assigned to infra-incident. Pager duty notified.

maya: observing successful connection handoffs; 60% of realtime traffic now on sfo1, latency for critical tenants within SLO so far.

samir: network provider still seeing intermittent flaps; recommended to keep syd1 isolated until provider confirms stable for 2 hours.

elaine: good work. Next: 1) stabilize sfo1 capacity 2) keep syd1 cordoned, collect kubelet + CNI + kernel logs, 3) postmortem owner assigned (maya).

maya: acknowledged. I'll collect logs and stash at s3://redwood-incident-logs/INC-4521/ and start postmortem draft.

sourav: will follow up on cost/teardown timeline. Recommend automatic teardown 12h after region marked stable.

deploy-bot: Action checklist updated: cordon done, traffic-shift at 60%, dedicated-burst active.

elaine: closing initial triage, moving to escalation channel #incidents-4521. Keep this thread for quick notes. :thumbsup:
